It was only set if "runtests.py" picked it up as a tag, which means that there couldn't be a space between the tags at the top of the file and the `distutils:` directives.

Specifically this was a problem for `extsubscript.py`, `lzss_compression.pyx`.

I've chosen to allow blank lines in front of tags (on the basis that it's an easy and invisible mistake to make). The alternative would be to fix the specific tests.

comment_data.body: This is to stop "ok:" being recognised as a tag
We could also ignore tags without value.
That works for `ok:` but not for `# NOTE: Py2.6+ only` or `# FIXME: don't know why this does not work on MacOS`

We could also only accept `distutils:` or `cython:` as tags once we've seen a blank line (on the basis that this matches how people are actually likely o use them). Although it's obviously heading a little bit into "complicated special-case"

> We could also only accept `distutils:` or `cython:` as tags once we've seen a blank line

Isn't there just a fixed list of some 4 or 5 valid tags? As soon as we spot a 'tag' that isn't a known 'tag', we can stop.

We shouldn't overdesign this, but it seems counterintuitive to me that an empty comment line should have a meaning at all and that it is used to stop tag processing.

There is a fixed list - it's in https://github.com/da-woods/cython/blob/42aba371ce7a7057dbda6b7b84c4b8d24cffdb70/runtests.py#L558 and it warns if something isn't in the fixed list. I think the warning is probably good thing.

I've added the pre-existing `NOTE:`, `FIXME:` and 'ok:' to the list of things that aren't treated as tags or warned about since I think they're clearly comments. That's feels like the most minimal thing to do that isn't overdesigning it.

(An empty comment line with still stop tag processing but that's pre-existing so I'm inclined not to change it - just not to actually use it)

commit.message:
Fix some "distutils: define_macros" not being set in tests

It was only set if "runtests.py" picked it up as a tag, which
means that there couldn't be a space between the tags at the
top of the file and the `distutils:` directives.

Specifically this was a problem for `extsubscript.py`,
`lzss_compression.pyx`.

I've chosen to allow blank lines in front of tags (on the basis
that it's an easy and invisible mistake to make). The alternative
would be to fix the specific tests.
Adjust tags parsing slightly to pass existing uses

title: Fix some "distutils: define_macros" not being set in tests
